target.title: fix(cli): shell completion omitted command aliases like capability, chat, and cron create
target.body:
Closes #99406

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with installed shell completion could not tab-complete any command alias: `openclaw --help` advertises `capability`, `chat`, and `terminal` as commands (and they run fine — `openclaw capability --help` prints `Usage: openclaw infer|capability ...`), but zsh/bash/fish/PowerShell completion never offered them, and typing an alias (`openclaw capability <TAB>`, `openclaw cron create <TAB>`) dead-ended completion for the rest of the command line. Eight registered aliases were affected (`capability`, `terminal`, `chat`, `exec-approvals`, `cron create`, `cron remove`, `cron delete`, `plugins info`).

## Why This Change Was Made

All four generators in `src/cli/completion-cli.ts` built their command lists, case dispatches, and path matchers exclusively from `command.name()` and never read `command.aliases()`. The fix adds two small helpers (`commandNameVariants`, `childPathVariants`) and makes each generator alias-aware in its own idiom: zsh and bash add alias names to the command lists and use multi-pattern case labels (`(infer|capability)`), while fish and PowerShell thread alias-expanded path variants through their recursive visitors so completion keeps working for the segments after an alias (`cron create <TAB>` now offers `cron add`'s options). `collectFishPathOptionFlags` also resolves alias path segments so fish value-option skip lists stay identical on alias paths. For programs without aliases the emitted scripts are byte-identical to before (verified against the pre-change generator across all four shells).

A pre-push review pass over the diff caught that the `exec-approvals` root alias was **dead at runtime**: commander registers it, but the lazy argv router only routes names owned by the sub-CLI group/descriptor catalogs, and the approvals group listed only `["approvals"]` — `openclaw exec-approvals --help` exited 1 with "Did you mean openclaw approvals" on current main. Advertising it in completion would have shipped a broken word, so this PR also wires the alias the same way the working aliases (`capability`, `terminal`, `chat`) are wired: added to the approvals group `commandNames`, a descriptor row, and a `command-catalog.ts` policy entry matching `approvals`. `openclaw exec-approvals --help` now exits 0 with `Usage: openclaw approvals|exec-approvals`.

Known cost, stated plainly: alias-path expansion grows the generated fish (+~8.5%) and PowerShell (+~14%) scripts for the real tree because aliased subtrees are emitted per path variant (zsh/bash grow <1%). Variants multiply by (1 + alias count) per aliased ancestor — no aliased command nests under another today. If maintainers prefer, a follow-up can make this linear by canonicalizing typed alias segments in the fish/PowerShell matchers instead of duplicating subtrees; the shared `childPathVariants` helper is the single place that change would land.

## User Impact

Tab completion now matches what the CLI accepts and what `--help` advertises: alias names complete at every level in all four supported shells, and completion continues normally after an alias. `openclaw exec-approvals` now works as a routed alias of `approvals` (it previously failed with "Unknown command") and appears in root help like the other alias rows. No other runtime behavior or flags changed. Users with a cached completion script get the fix through the existing regeneration paths (`openclaw completion --install`, update-time cache refresh, doctor).

## Evidence

Regression tests fail without the fix (4 new per-shell tests, red on the unfixed generator):

```text
❯ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/completion-cli.test.ts   # before fix
 × completes root and nested aliases in zsh lists and dispatch
 × completes root and nested aliases in bash word lists and case labels
 × completes aliases and their subtrees in fish
 × completes aliases and alias command paths in PowerShell
 Tests  4 failed | 8 passed (12)
❯ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/completion-cli.test.ts   # after fix
 Tests  12 passed (12)
```

Real command tree, generator driven directly from source (same eager registration `openclaw completion` uses), before vs after:

```text
                          pre-fix   post-fix
'capability[...]'  entries   0         1
'terminal[...]'              0         1
'chat[...]'                  0         1
'exec-approvals[...]'        0         1
'create[Add a cron job]'     0         1
'create[...]' total          4         5   (the 4 are genuine subcommands named create; unchanged)
```

Built CLI end-to-end: regenerated all four shells' scripts; zsh script contains the alias entries plus dispatch lines `(infer|capability) _openclaw_infer ;;`, `(add|create) _openclaw_cron_add ;;`, and `(approvals|exec-approvals) _openclaw_approvals ;;`; `zsh -n` and `bash -n` both pass on the generated output.

Routing before/after on the built CLI:

```console
# before (main)
$ openclaw exec-approvals --help
Unknown command: openclaw exec-approvals
Did you mean this?
  openclaw approvals        # exit 1
# after (this branch)
$ openclaw exec-approvals --help | head -1
Usage: openclaw approvals|exec-approvals [options] [command]   # exit 0
```

Validation run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on all completion suites plus the routing-adjacent suites (`completion-cli`, `completion-fish`, `completion-runtime`, `completion-cli.write-state`, `register.subclis`, `subcli-descriptors`, `help`, `command-registry`, `exec-approvals-cli`): 65/65 pass, including a new regression test that dispatches `openclaw exec-approvals` through the approvals registrar (mirroring the existing infer/capability test).
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on touched files; `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` green.
- Existing-output compatibility: for alias-free programs the visitors emit in the same order as before (all pre-existing completion tests pass unchanged).

AI-assisted: authored with Claude (Claude Code); verification (red/green tests, source-driven before/after dumps, generated-script syntax checks) executed and reviewed as described above.
